summary.headline: Shalibhadra Finance FY26 AUM rose 25% to ₹220 crore and PAT grew 21.67% to ₹19.48 crore; FY29 target is ₹500 crore AUM.
summary.overview: Management hosted its inaugural earnings call covering Q4 and FY26. AUM closed FY26 at ₹220 crore (up 25% from ₹176 crore), PAT rose 21.67% YoY to ₹19.48 crore, with ROA of 8.65% and ROE of 11.33%. GNPA stood at 2.94%, CRAR at 78.28%, and net worth at ₹172 crore. The company is moving from two-wheeler and vehicle finance into micro-LAP, LAP and home loans under its "Shalibhadra 2.0" strategy, with a branch expansion from 61 toward 100 branches. Management guided to lower ROA (about 7% within two to three years) and a rising share of nationalised bank borrowing to cut funding costs.

financial_highlights.value: ~₹50 crore, of which ~₹20 crore from nationalised banks (~40%)

segments.name: Two-wheeler and vehicle finance
segments.commentary: Core book, described as nearly 100% secured; management says over 95% of the current portfolio is two-wheelers. Company estimates it finances about 60% of vehicles sold in its operating geographies.

segments.name: Micro-LAP, LAP and home loans
segments.commentary: Launched in FY26 as new segments with higher ticket sizes. Target customers are salaried or government employees, or borrowers with agricultural assets, CIBIL above 700, and low leverage. Credit cost expected near 1% versus about 2% for two-wheelers.

segments.name: Salaried personal loan and used-vehicle cross-sell
segments.commentary: Newer products cross-sold to existing customers; about 40% of new loans go to existing customers, drawn from roughly 5 lakh credit-worthy customers.

guidance_outlook: FY29 AUM target of ₹500 crore, with management saying it is achievable within three years; ₹1,000 crore possible in about five years if everything goes right.
No equity dilution needed until ₹1,000 crore AUM, funded through NCDs and term loans.
Branches to rise from 61 to 70 by calendar 2026, 75 by year-end and 85 next year, targeting 100 by FY29 at about one branch per month.
Expected ROA to fall to about 7% within two to three years as the LAP and home-loan mix rises.
Nationalised bank share of borrowings targeted at 50-60%, with 60% by around FY29; nationalised banks lend at roughly 10-10.5%.
Expected automatic two-notch credit rating upgrade once AUM reaches ₹500 crore, per management's reading of market practice.
Target product mix in three years: two-wheelers 60%, newer products 40%. At ₹500 crore AUM, about ₹300 crore from existing products and ₹200 crore from new products.
capex_capacity: Capex per new branch about ₹20 lakh (₹15 lakh real estate, ₹5 lakh furniture, opening and staffing); breakeven at about ₹50 lakh AUM within 1-1.5 years.
Branch network at 61; target 100 by FY29 with selective entry into Karnataka and Goa.
Recent expansion focus: Saurashtra (Gujarat), Bhopal region (Madhya Pradesh), and Nagpur, Akola, Amravati and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Maharashtra).
Technology investment in proprietary LOS and LMS platforms; management says underwriting is almost 100% automated.
Management says no branch has been closed; underperforming branches can take two to three years to mature.
demand_pricing: Lending rates are fixed at origination, so RBI rate moves affect spread through borrowing costs rather than yields.
Yield on advances fell from 25.4% (FY24) to 20.8% (FY26), attributed to competition from new entrants, a market-wide decline in lending rates and lower pricing for customers with good bureau scores.
Management expects some spread pressure from competition over the next two to three years.
Around 70% of customers are new-to-credit; the company uses informal assessment (land, cash flow, Mandi and milk-cooperative receipts, village references).
Management sees large rural demand (about 70% of the population in rural areas) with few lenders.
Monthly OEM sales data is used to choose branch locations and to grow AUM at existing branches.

qa_highlights.question: What credit cost do you expect in LAP and home loans versus two-wheeler loans?
qa_highlights.answer: Current two-wheeler credit cost is about 2%; mortgage loans are expected at about 1% because property is immovable and easier to repossess.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the book comes from repeat borrowers?
qa_highlights.answer: About 40% of new loans and about 40% of AUM are to existing customers, drawn from roughly 5 lakh credit-worthy customers.

qa_highlights.question: How will ROA and NIMs change as the mix shifts to LAP and home loans?
qa_highlights.answer: ROA is 8.65% now and is expected to fall to about 7% in two to three years as higher-ticket products rise.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company bring down its cost of funds, given the 12% NCD?
qa_highlights.answer: The 12% coupon was the first NCD issue; costs are expected to fall as the company gains experience and the nationalised bank share rises (lending at about 10-10.5%).

qa_highlights.question: What is the branch rollout schedule and capex per branch?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is 70 branches by calendar 2026, 75 by year-end, 85 next year, and 100 by FY29; capex is about ₹20 lakh per branch with breakeven in 1-1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why has yield on advances fallen from 25.4% to 20.8%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites competition from new entrants, lower market lending rates, and discounted rates for customers with good credit bureau scores.

risks_watch: Agricultural income dependence: drought or irregular rainfall could raise NPAs and slow growth, per management.
Spread compression from new entrants and falling yields; ROA guided down from 8.65% toward 7%.
Funding concentration and cost: borrowings are only about ₹50 crore, and the NCD was raised at 12% against a stated cost of funds of about 11%.
Execution of the branch ramp (61 to 100) into new states such as Karnataka and Goa where brand recall is absent.
New-product credit performance in LAP and home loans, which lack operating history at the company; management targets NNPA around 1% for the next two to three years.
Rate-cycle exposure: an RBI hike would raise borrowing costs while lending rates stay fixed.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, capital and technology, but cautious and sometimes hedged on margins and ROA, which management concedes will fall. Answers on borrowing costs and the 1,000 crore timeline were less specific, and the call was a first-time event with limited quantitative detail.
key_quotes: Till 1,000 crores of AUM, we do not need any further equity dilution.
So, if we reach 500 crores, there will be an automatic increase of two notches in credit rating.
So, within next two to three years, we expect it to be around 7%.

adds.what: Branch network 61 to 70 by calendar 2026, 75 by year-end, 85 next year, 100 by FY29 (about 1 branch/month, ~36 branches in 36 months)

growth.why: Management targets AUM of ₹500 crore by FY29 (from ₹220 crore, ~2.3x) backed by a branch rollout from 61 to 100 at about one branch per month, with 70 branches by calendar 2026; PAT grew 21.67% YoY but guided ROA is falling toward ~7%, and the new micro-LAP/LAP/home-loan products are not yet quantified with orders.
